extracted.intended_audience: debt collectors, compliance officers, consumer-finance attorneys, and regulated entities subject to Regulation F/FDCPA
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and compliance standards for debt-collection communications under Regulation F and the FDCPA, focusing on telephone-call frequency limits, permitted/excluded communications, required disclosures, and prohibited means (including social media, mail, and email). Useful for practitioners implementing or evaluating collector conduct and policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone-call frequency presumption of compliance (§1006.14(b)(2)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector is presumed to comply with §1006.14(b)(1) and FDCPA section 806(5) if the debt collector's telephone call frequencies do not exceed the telephone call frequencies described in §1006.14(b)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate application (e.g., multiple unanswered calls to a third party within seven days may still produce a presumption of compliance). See §1006.10(c) for further guidance about communications with third parties for location information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that may rebut presumption of compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a collector's call frequencies fall within the limits of §1006.14(b)(2)(i), the presumption of compliance may be rebutted by proof the collector nonetheless placed calls or engaged in conversation repeatedly or continuously with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exhaustive factors (may be considered alone or in combination) include: (i) frequency and pattern of calls (e.g., rapid succession or high concentration, such as two unanswered calls within five minutes or seven calls in one day); (ii) frequency and pattern of voicemails; (iii) content of prior communications (e.g., prior statements the person did not want to be contacted, cease-communication notices under §1006.6(c), or §1006.14(h) requests not to use telephone calls); and (iv) the debt collector's conduct in prior communications (e.g., obscene/abusive language, threats, calling at an inconvenient time). The amount of time since prior communications may be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Misdirected telephone calls not counted toward person-specific frequencies
rubrics_metrics.description: If, within seven consecutive days, a collector places calls to a number and later learns that the number is not that person's number, those calls are not considered telephone calls placed to that person for purposes of §1006.14(b)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: calls placed on Monday and Wednesday to a number later learned on Thursday to belong to someone else are not considered calls to the consumer during that seven-day period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of violation when call frequencies exceeded (§1006.14(b)(2)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector is presumed to violate §1006.14(b)(1) and FDCPA section 806(5) if the collector places a telephone call to a person in connection with collection of a particular debt in excess of either of the telephone call frequencies described in §1006.14(b)(2)(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show concrete violations (e.g., eight telephone calls in seven days where none are excluded by §1006.14(b)(3) leads to a presumption of violation; a post-conversation call before seven days may also create a presumption of violation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors that may rebut presumption of violation
rubrics_metrics.description: A presumption of violation based on exceeding the frequencies may be rebutted by proving the collector did not act with intent to annoy, abuse, or harass despite exceeding the frequencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exhaustive factors include: (i) whether the call was made to comply with or as required by applicable law (e.g., loss-mitigation notices under Regulation X); (ii) whether the call was directly related to active litigation (court-ordered communications or settlement negotiations); (iii) whether the call was in response to a consumer's request for additional information (where prior-consent exclusion did not apply at the time); and (iv) whether the call conveyed information that would provide the consumer an opportunity to avoid a demonstrably negative effect where time was of the essence (with examples illustrating when time-sensitive consumer-benefit calls may or may not rebut the presumption). It is assumed collectors intend the natural consequences of their actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-consent exclusion for telephone-call frequencies (§1006.14(b)(3)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: Telephone calls a debt collector places to a person who gives prior consent directly to the collector are excluded from the telephone call frequencies described in §1006.14(b)(2), subject to other prohibitions (e.g., §§1006.6(b) and 1006.14(h) still apply).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a person gives prior consent for additional calls about a particular debt, calls placed thereafter about that debt do not count toward the frequencies for up to seven consecutive days. Prior consent may expire earlier if (1) the person consented for a shorter period, (2) the person revokes consent, or (3) the collector has a telephone conversation with the person about the debt. Examples illustrate calls permitted under consent and limits when consent is not renewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unconnected telephone calls excluded from frequency counts (§1006.14(b)(3)(ii))
rubrics_metrics.description: A call does not count toward the telephone-call frequencies if it does not connect to the dialed number (e.g., busy signal or indication the number is not in service).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversely, a call counts if it connects: e.g., if answered (even if it drops), if it causes the phone to ring at the dialed number but no one answers, or if it connects to voicemail or another recorded message (even without ringing or leaving a voicemail).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and counting rules for 'particular debt' (§1006.14(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for student loans, 'particular debt' means each of a consumer's debts in collection. For student loans, 'particular debt' means all student loan debts serviced under a single account number at the time obtained by a debt collector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under §1006.14(b)(2)(i)(A)-(B): a call that initiates a conversation or leaves a voicemail about one debt counts for that debt; if the call discusses multiple debts, it counts for each such debt. An unanswered call or a call that leaves a non-specific limited-content message may be counted toward at least one particular debt. Numerous examples illustrate counting when multiple debts are being collected (e.g., how to allocate unanswered calls or general conversations across multiple debts, and the special rule treating multiple student loans under one account as a single debt for counting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using communication media a person has requested not to use (§1006.14(h)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector is prohibited from communicating or attempting to communicate with a person through a medium of communication if the person has requested the collector not use that medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector may ask follow-up questions to clarify preferred media. Within a medium, a person can specify particular addresses or phone numbers not to be used (e.g., asking to stop calling means telephone calls are prohibited thereafter). Opt-out of electronic communications at a particular email or number prohibits use of that address or number for any debt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception where communication medium is legally required (§1006.14(h)(2)(iii))
rubrics_metrics.description: If otherwise required by applicable law, a debt collector may communicate through a medium the person requested not to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a mortgage servicer subject to Regulation Z periodic statement requirements may still mail periodic statements even if the person asked the collector to stop mailing letters (unless the consumer consented to electronic statements per Reg Z).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on false or deceptive representations or means (including social media) (§1006.18(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector may not use any false representation or deceptive means to collect a debt or to obtain information concerning a consumer; this prohibition applies in social media contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (i) sending a private social-media message requesting to be added as a contact without disclosing identity as a debt collector is a false representation/implication; (ii) when communicating privately with a friend or coworker to acquire location information, the collector must identify himself or herself individually by name (and comply with §1006.10 and §1006.6(d)(1) and social-media-specific rules in §1006.22(f)(4)). See also commentary regarding assumed names (§1006.18(f)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited-content messages and disclosure obligations (§1006.18(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A limited-content message, as defined in §1006.2(j), is not a 'communication' under §1006.2(d), so a collector leaving only a limited-content message need not make the disclosures required by §1006.18(e)(1) and (2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a voicemail includes content beyond the limited-content message content and directly or indirectly conveys information regarding a debt, the voicemail is a 'communication' and the collector must make the §1006.18(e) disclosures. See the commentary to §1006.2(d) and (j) for clarification of definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-communication disclosure requirement (§1006.18(e)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must make the disclosure required by §1006.18(e)(1) in the collector's initial communication with a consumer, regardless of medium and who initiated the communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: If a collector leaves a limited-content message and the consumer then calls the collector, that consumer-initiated call is the initial communication and the collector must disclose during that call that it is attempting to collect a debt and that information obtained will be used for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translated disclosures must match the language(s) used in communication (§1006.18(e)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A collector must make the disclosures required by §1006.18(e)(1) and (2) in the same language(s) used for the rest of the communication in which the disclosures are conveyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: if the initial communication occurs in Spanish, the §1006.18(e)(1) disclosure must be in Spanish. If a later communication mixes English and Spanish, the §1006.18(e)(2) disclosure must be provided in both languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of assumed names permitted if collector can readily identify employee (§1006.18(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee may use an assumed name when communicating or attempting to communicate, provided the debt collector can readily identify any employee using an assumed name.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collector may manage assumed names by requiring an employee to use the same assumed name for all communications and prohibiting other employees from using the same assumed name, or any other method that enables the collector to determine the employee's true identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on language or symbols on mail envelopes (§1006.22(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector must not use any language or symbol, other than the debt collector's address, on any envelope when communicating with a consumer by mail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The phrase 'language or symbol' does not include language/symbols that facilitate mail communications, such as the debtor's name/address, postage, 'forwarding and address correction requested', and USPS Intelligent Mail barcodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on emailing employer-provided addresses (§1006.22(f)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A debt collector generally must not communicate or attempt to communicate with a consumer by sending an email to an email address the collector knows is provided to the consumer by the consumer's employer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a general prohibition; collectors should avoid using employer-provided email addresses to contact consumers for debt collection purposes.
